description: Simulate year-by-year retirement withdrawals against investment returns and inflation, and see how long the money lasts.

faqs.a: Each year: balance grows by the investment return, then the withdrawal (raised by inflation) is taken out. The table runs until the balance hits zero or 60 years pass.
Withdrawals rise with inflation each year to preserve purchasing power, while the remaining balance keeps earning the assumed return.
faqs.q: How do inflation and returns interact?

faqs.a: The classic rule of thumb withdraws 4% of the starting balance in year one (then inflation-adjusted). Use it as the annual withdrawal input to test the rule on your numbers.

howto: Enter your starting balance and annual withdrawal amount.
Set expected investment return and inflation.
Read how many years the money lasts and scan the yearly table.
keywords: how long will my retirement last
title: Retirement Withdrawal Calculator
